title: Same clay, now it floats?
hook: A lump of clay sinks. Same clay, new shape: how much water must it shove aside to float?

knows: some things float and some sink
doesNotKnow: that shape changes how much water an object can displace

misconception: Heavy things sink and light things float; changing the shape of the same material cannot make it float.
objective: The learner can explain that a floating object pushes aside its own weight of water, and that a hollow shape lets the same heavy material do that.

claims.text: The upward push of water on an object equals the weight of the water it pushes aside (Archimedes' principle); a floating object pushes aside its own weight of water.
claims.source: Archimedes' principle; Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 14 (fluids).

claims.text: 1 kg of fresh water has a volume of 1.00 L, so a floating 1 kg object pushes aside 1.00 L.
claims.source: Fresh water density 1000 kg/m^3 (about 20 C; 998 kg/m^3 exactly, idealised as 1000). 1 kg / 1000 kg/m^3 = 0.001 m^3 = 1 L.

claims.text: 1 kg of clay at about 1800 kg/m^3 has a volume of 0.56 L, so as a sunken ball it pushes aside only 0.56 L.
claims.source: 1 / 1800 m^3 = 0.000556 m^3 = 0.556 L. Clay density 1800 kg/m^3 is a typical value for wet modelling clay, stated as approximate (brief cm-physics #11).

claims.text: The stage draws to scale four open cylindrical cups of 1 kg of clay with outer volumes 0.80, 1.25, 1.80 and 2.50 L; the 0.80 L cup sinks, and the others float with 5.9, 4.0 and 2.8 cm deep (below the waterline). A 'Tried' line lists each shape the learner has shown and the water it pushes aside.
claims.source: Unchanged numbers (fact-check pass 11: cup() gives D = 11.93/14.71/17.89/21.29 cm; drafts 5.88, 3.98, 2.81 cm). Revision v4: the stage adds a 'Tried:' line and the reveal quotes the small cup only if the learner showed it. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 14): Own node copy of cup(): D = 11.93/14.71/17.89/21.29 cm, H = 7.16/7.36/7.16/7.02 cm, clay 555.6 cm^3 each; drafts 1000/(pi D^2/4) = 8.95 (but hull 0.80 L < 1 L, sinks), 5.88, 3.98, 2.81 cm, each below its height. 'Tried' line uses pushed(): 0.56 L for ball/small cup, 1.00 L for floaters.

claims.text: A cup that sinks fills with water and then pushes aside only its clay, 0.56 L.
claims.source: Once flooded, the only volume excluding water is the clay itself (0.556 L).

claims.text: Clay is heavier than water litre for litre, so a solid lump of it never pushes aside enough water to float.
claims.source: Solid lump displaces its own volume V; buoyancy 1000 g V < weight 1800 g V for any V.

recall.question: A 3 kg steel pot floats in a sink of fresh water. How much water is it pushing aside?
options: Less than 1 L, steel is dense
It depends on the pot's shape
recall.why: A floating object pushes aside its own weight of water: 3 kg of water is 3 L, whatever the shape.
